# dsh-terminal-keybar-dock

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Client plugin: the
mobile twin of
dsh-terminal-keybar, without the
floating

Seek Harness (DSH) Client plugin: the
mobile twin of
dsh-terminal-keybar, without the
floating look.

A phone's soft keyboard has no Escape, Tab, Ctrl, Shift or arrow keys, and the DSH
terminal has no o

n-screen replacement. The upstream plugin floats a translucent
column of those keys beside the termi
nal; this variant **docks** them instead:

- a **solid horizontal bar** along the bottom edge of the active terminal — on
a phone the right Sid

the terminal gives the bar its band**: the body box holding the terminal
reserves a bottom padding o

f the bar's height (plus the keyboard inset while
the keyboard is open), so the terminal re-fits abo

**rides the soft keyboard**: while the keyboard is open the bar sits directly
on top of it, tracking

/ Shift modifiers**: the two keys at the head of the row are sticky and
apply to the next bar key or

the next character typed on the soft keyboard, so
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R — the reason a terminal

has Ctrl — become reachable;
- **mobile only, and only while the terminal is on screen**: it appears

on touch
devices with a viewport narrower than 768px while the right Sidebar's active
tab is a term

inal and that terminal's body is actually visible. On tablets and
landscape phones (side-by-side lay

out) it stays off, and collapsing the panel
takes the bar with it.
## Modifier keys (Ctrl / Shift)

The `Ctrl` and `Shift` keys are **sticky, one-shot modifiers**: tap one and it
lights up, tap it aga

in to cancel, and the two compose (Ctrl+Shift). An armed
modifier applies to the **next key** — a ba

r key or one character typed on the
soft keyboard — and then clears itself.

- **Against the bar**: `Shift`+`Tab` sends `ESC [ Z` (back-tab), and `Ctrl` /
`Shift` + an arrow sen

ds the standard xterm modifier sequence (`ESC [ 1 ; 5 A`
for Ctrl+↑, `1;2` for Shift, `1;6` for both

), so Ctrl+←/→ moves by word in
readline and vim. `Ctrl`+`Esc`, `Ctrl`+`↵` and `Ctrl`+`^C` send the

same bytes
as the unmodified keys — terminals draw no further distinction.
- **Against the soft keyb

oard**: while a modifier is armed, the next typed
character is intercepted from the terminal's hidde

n textarea as a cancelable
`beforeinput`, the insertion is cancelled, and the rewritten byte goes th

rough
the same terminal service. Ctrl+A…Z become the C0 control bytes (Ctrl+C
interrupt, Ctrl+D EOF,

Ctrl+Z suspend, Ctrl+R reverse search, Ctrl+L clear,
Ctrl+W kill word); Ctrl+`[ \ ] ^ _`, space and

`?` map to their ASCII control
codes; Shift uppercases ASCII letters. Input that is not one keystro

ke — an IME
composition, a paste — is left alone and the modifiers stay armed.
- Tapping anywhere ou

tside the bar, switching tabs or the bar disappearing clears
the armed state, so a modifier tapped b

y accident cannot rewrite a later
keystroke.

Shift only changes the case of ASCII letters; digits and symbols keep whatever
the soft keyboard's o

wn Shift produced (layouts differ, and the plugin does not
guess). Ctrl sends a character with no co
ntrol meaning exactly as typed.
## How the keyboard inset works

iOS Safari and modern Android Chrome keep the layout viewport intact and shrink
`window.visualViewpo

rt` instead, so a plain `position: fixed; bottom: 0` bar
would sit behind the keyboard. The bar read

s the keyboard inset as
`innerHeight − visualViewport.offsetTop − visualViewport.height` and sets it

s own
`bottom` to `max(inset, env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` — on the keyboard while it
is open, abov

e the home indicator while it is closed. The reserved band the
terminal gives up is the same express

ion plus the bar's height, so the terminal's
bottom edge always meets the bar's top edge. Browsers t

hat resize the layout
viewport instead (older Android, Firefox) report no inset and need none: their
`bottom: 0` is already above the keyboard.

Presses use `pointerdown` with `preventDefault`, so the terminal's textarea keeps
focus and the soft

keyboard stays open. Bytes go through the public Client
terminal service of the active tab (`webTer

minals.view(...).write(...)`); no
terminal code is copied.
## Install

Install as a local bundle from this directory (DeepSeek Harness, Plugins →
Install, or the `plugin_m

anager` tool with `install_bundle`). Then **disable the
upstream `dsh-terminal-keybar`** so the floa

ting column does not appear beside
the docked bar. Reload the page after installation.
## Notes

- Derived from `dsh-terminal-keybar` (MIT); the write path, seat registration
and diagnosis badge ar

e inherited from it, while the sticky Ctrl/Shift
modifiers and typed-character interception are new

here. See `MAINTENANCE.md`
for every upstream API this plugin touches — including the tab-body marke

rs the
visibility gate and the reserved band are built on, and the hidden textarea the
modifiers int

ercept.
- The keyboard-inset path follows the standard `visualViewport` formula, which
desktop brows

ers cannot fully exercise (no soft keyboard); the closed-keyboard
docked layout, the reserved band a

nd key delivery are verifiable in a narrow
touch-emulated viewport, the open-keyboard ride-up needs

a real phone. The
modifier interception listens for `beforeinput`, which a touch-emulated page
can d
ispatch; the real soft-keyboard timing still deserves a pass on a phone.
